BEHIND THE EXPERIENCE

One storefront. Clear responsibilities.

Next.js is the shop customers see.
Each connected service has a specific job.

GIDENTITY

Google

Verifies who’s signing in.

MCOMMERCE CORE

Medusa

Manages customers, products, carts and orders.

OBUSINESS CONTACTS

Odoo

Keeps customer contacts available to the business.

mMARKETING

Mautic

Manages marketing contacts and email preferences.

ZCUSTOMER SUPPORT

Zammad

Turns contact messages into support tickets.

FOLLOW A CUSTOMER JOURNEY

From the action on screen to the service behind it.

A simple shopping experience.

The storefront presents the collection; Medusa handles the commerce data.

  1. 01
    Next.js storefront

    Browse jewelry in English or Spanish.

  2. 02
    Medusa commerce

    Load products and prices, manage the cart and submit checkout.

  3. 03
    Customer account

    Find order history and manage profile and addresses.

Where does the catalog come from?

Medusa supplies live commerce data. Example catalog items are for browsing and cannot be checked out. Odoo product/catalog sync is disabled in the current configuration; the Odoo integration here is for customer contacts.

Google proves identity. Medusa owns the account.

Customers can use Google or email and password to access their store account.

  1. 01
    Continue with Google

    Google authenticates the customer through Medusa’s Google provider.

  2. 02
    Complete the account

    New customers accept Terms and Privacy before their Medusa customer account is created.

  3. 03
    Return to the shop

    The storefront keeps the session in a secure HttpOnly cookie.

What if the customer already has an account?

A matching Google email does not automatically take over a password account. Customers must prove their existing password to link it. Customer sign-in is separate from staff access, and marketing email remains an optional choice.

Customer details flow to the right tools.

Medusa is the source for store customer profiles. Background delivery keeps business tools in step.

  1. 01
    Save in Medusa

    Profile changes and marketing choices are recorded with durable sync work.

  2. 02
    Update Odoo + Mautic

    Odoo receives customer contact details; Mautic receives contact and marketing preference updates.

  3. 03
    Respect the choice

    Marketing eligibility follows consent and suppression rules. Mautic opt-outs flow back to the application.

Does a slow business tool hold up signup?

Odoo and Mautic delivery runs in the background, with retries and reconciliation. Signup does not wait for those remote tools. Newsletter-only signup goes to Mautic without creating a store account or Odoo contact. Having a customer record is not permission to send marketing.

A message becomes a ticket.

The contact form connects customers directly to the support workflow.

  1. 01
    Send a message

    The customer fills out the storefront contact form.

  2. 02
    Validate on the server

    The contact API checks the request; Redis limits abuse and duplicate submissions.

  3. 03
    Create a Zammad ticket

    The team handles the request in its support queue. Zammad sends the acknowledgement.

How are retries and replies handled?

Successful identical messages are deduplicated for 24 hours. An uncertain delivery stays pending for reconciliation. Replies to the acknowledgement alias are not automatically added to Zammad; customers can use the contact form with their ticket reference. Support works independently of commerce demo mode.

THE HARDWARE BEHIND ANTALOS

MY HOMELAB

A compact rack. A place to build, break, and learn.
Repurposed hardware connects virtualization, storage, and a segmented network.

SMALL FOOTPRINT, MANY ROLES

A physical home for the virtual stack.

My NavePoint rack brings a dedicated firewall, managed switching, shared storage, and three Proxmox hosts together. Two compact Lenovo edge servers sit side by side, while a repurposed HP Omen adds GPU compute.

Buying used, repairing hardware, and reusing parts make the lab an exercise in resourcefulness as much as system administration. A Cat6 patch panel keeps the wiring organized; an APC UPS and rack PDU handle power.

3
Proxmox hosts
112 GB
combined host RAM
10 GbE
SFP+ service links

01 / HARDWARE

Each machine has a job.

ROUTING + SWITCHING

The network foundation

OPNsense runs on a Beikong H31F with an Intel N150, 8 GB RAM, three 2.5 GbE ports, and two SFP+ ports. A Juniper EX3300-24T provides 24 gigabit copper ports and four 10 GbE SFP+ ports.

Dedicated firewall · Managed switching

VIRTUALIZATION

2 × ThinkSystem SE350

Each Lenovo node has a Xeon D-2143IT with 8 cores / 16 threads and 48 GB ECC RAM. Proxmox divides these machines into Talos Kubernetes nodes, Debian workloads, and HAProxy VMs.

96 GB ECC RAM across the pair

GPU COMPUTE

Repurposed HP Omen

An Intel Core i7-9700KF and 16 GB RAM give this host a second life. The VM plan assigns an RTX 3060 with 12 GB VRAM to Debian for LLM inference, alongside Talos control and worker VMs.

GPU passthrough · Dedicated inference VM

STORAGE + POWER

A dedicated TrueNAS server

A Ryzen 3 2200G powers the 2U, four-bay NAS with separate gigabit management and SFP+ connectivity. An APC SUA1500 UPS, AP9630 network card, and 12-outlet PDU round out the supporting hardware.

Shared storage · Networked UPS management

02 / NETWORK DESIGN

Separate the traffic by purpose.

Management uses dedicated gigabit access links on VLAN 20. The Proxmox hosts carry internal and DMZ service traffic over 10 GbE trunks on VLANs 30 and 40.

From the internet to the rack

  1. UPLINKAT&T gatewayInternet connection
  2. ROUTE + FILTEROPNsenseVLAN routing and firewall
  3. DISTRIBUTEJuniper EX3300Access ports and tagged trunks
1 GbE / VLAN 20
Management plane

Proxmox, Lenovo XCC, TrueNAS, and UPS management interfaces.

10 GbE / VLANs 30 + 40
Service plane

Proxmox VM networks use SFP+ trunks. TrueNAS also connects over SFP+ for storage traffic.

Simplified topology · VLAN roles describe the network plan; firewall policy determines access between segments.

VLAN 10

Clients

VLAN 20

VLAN 40

DMZ

VLAN 50

VLAN 60

VLAN 100

Work apps

A separate network for work applications.

03 / FROM MACHINES TO SERVICES

Proxmox → Talos → Antalos

The VM worksheet places one Talos control VM and one worker VM on each of the three hosts. The Lenovo nodes also host two HAProxy DMZ VMs and Debian workloads for testing, Jellyfin, and Immich machine learning, with an Intel Arc A310 assigned to the media VM.

This is where physical networking meets the application stack: Proxmox supplies the virtual machines, Talos runs Kubernetes, and Antalos defines the services above it.
